collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Someone laughs out loud at a burial at a happy memory: laugh along, or ask them to be quiet.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At the burial of Old Auntie Pip, the funniest woman on Isola, (subject) suddenly remembers the time Auntie Pip hid a crab in the elders' meeting hut, and laughs out loud. Everyone turns. (friend), Auntie Pip's daughter, stares at (subject). What should (friend) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) starts to laugh too. Then someone else remembers the crab, and then the time with the coconut and the eldest elder's hat, and before long the whole burial is in fits. Auntie Pip is buried to the sound of the whole village laughing. It is exactly right.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks (subject), tightly, to be quiet. (subject) apologizes. The burial goes on in silence. Later, (friend) comes to find (subject) and asks (subject.him/her) to tell the crab story properly. They both end up laughing and crying at once.
